<description>
{
 "summary": "Improves the FuzzedSock mock to assign distinct socket descriptors per socket and to realistically simulate operating system event reporting during socket waits. It adds support for partial event occurrences, urgent data, and connection reset failures with bounded receive buffers. Additionally, it instruments FuzzedSock to track I/O calls and asserts socket handling invariants within the connman fuzz target.",
 "problem": "Previously, FuzzedSock only assigned one of two descriptor values, leading CConnman::SocketHandler() to merge wait entries across different peers and process one peer's socket using another's events. Furthermore, FuzzedSock waits only ever reported all or none of the requested events, preventing fuzzers from exercising error handling for urgent data, partial ready events, or broken connections.",
 "evidence": [
  "Commit 8f8246e56d explains: 'every FuzzedSock had one of two socket values and CConnman::SocketHandler() merged the entries of different peers in a single wait, which led the connman fuzz target to act on one peer with the events of another.'",
  "Commit ca8aeff1c9 notes: 'FuzzedSock::Wait() and WaitMany() reported either nothing or exactly the requested events. The real OS reports more than that, and the fuzz targets never exercised the callers on it...'"
 ],

<category name="tests" title="Test infrastructure">
## Covers

The machinery of testing rather than tests of a particular area: the
functional test framework and runner, unit test utilities, the fuzzing
harnesses and corpora, benchmarks, linters, sanitizer configuration,
and fixes for flaky tests whose cause is in the framework. A test that
pins the behavior of one area (a wallet migration test, a p2p relay
test) belongs to that area, not here. The Tests and Fuzzing labels are
a prior, but a labeled PR whose tests are about one area goes to that
area instead.

## What matters here

Signal first: fixes for flaky or misleading tests, since a red CI that
nobody trusts hides real failures. Then coverage of high-risk code paths
that the fuzzers or functional tests do not reach, especially
consensus, mempool policy, and p2p message handling. Then framework
capabilities that unblock tests other areas need. Then test speed, which
every contributor pays for on every run. Then cleanliness of the test
code.

Adding tests for their own sake ranks low; adding a test that catches a
realistic regression ranks high.
